typography._comment: Deliberate divergence, not drift — documenting *why* a value differs. The base semantic/typography.json scale was bumped for Android/Portal's 10-foot TV viewing distance (a real legibility audit finding: 14-17px body/caption text is phone-fine-print-sized when read from a couch). Web is read at arm's length (desktop/phone browser), where that floor doesn't apply — this override pins web back to its own already-tuned sizes rather than inheriting the TV bump. contactName needs no override: it was already large enough for both contexts. badge has no override anymore: it's pinned to 10px in the base scale itself now (explicit user request, overriding an earlier TV-legibility argument for keeping it larger there) — same value on both platforms already, nothing left to diverge. statusRow gets the same pin as caption (14px) — web's status checklist was already sized right at arm's length before Android's TV-driven statusRow role existed; only Android needed the reduction. display has no override anymore either, for the same reason as badge: the base scale itself was pinned to 24 (user request, 2026-10-11, titles matching web) — nothing left to diverge there either.

size._comment: backButton: the on-screen Back button's own square size — originally measured to match the title's exact cap height (18px), then bumped on explicit user request (2026-10-11: 24px for 'make button and arrow larger', then 32px). Title is 24px, so this is a button-height:title-fontSize ratio of ~1.33 — coincidentally the same ratio Android's own Back button landed on (32dp button / 24sp title) despite the two being sized by entirely separate mechanisms. .back-button svg is a percentage of this, so the arrow grows with it too. Deliberately platform-specific like typography.display above: Android sizes its own Back button from its icon + padding directly (MainActivity.kt), not from this shared token at all, since the two platforms' titles never shared a font size or file to measure a cap height against in the first place.
